errorCodes.meaning: The oracle holds no key for the epoch this record was sealed under. `details.reason` says why, exactly as `rooms/keys/file-key` 0.2 says it: `notDelivered` — the room has moved to an epoch whose commit has not reached the oracle yet, so retrying after it arrives may succeed, and `details.heldEpoch`, when present, is the latest epoch the oracle holds; `beyondChain` — the oracle's epoch chain reaches back only to `details.earliestEpoch`; `removed` — a commit the oracle processed removed its principal from the room's group at `details.removedAtEpoch`, and the record's epoch is at or after it and below the epoch the principal next joined at, if it has, so no later commit will make it openable and catching up will not help.
The record failed authentication — it was sealed under a different key, or relocated.

purpose.description: The purpose the request named, when it named one.

purposeNamed.description: Whether the request named a purpose. False when it named none where more than one is granted.

errorCodes.meaning: The request names a purpose that is not granted, or names none where more than one is granted — by the caller's authorization at the key holder or by the principal's authority over the room. The refusal discloses no content and is distinct from `permissionDenied`, which refuses access itself (VTI-ACL-104).

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

Purpose.description: What content is used for: a lowerCamelCase name registered in the VTI specification's purpose registry (Appendix H) — `personalisation`, `taskExecution`, `analytics`, `modelTraining` at the time of writing — or an absolute IRI naming a purpose defined elsewhere, such as a purpose of the W3C Data Privacy Vocabulary (`https://w3id.org/dpv#ServicePersonalisation`). Compared by exact string equality: a consumer MUST NOT treat a purpose it does not recognise as equal to any other, and grants only a request naming exactly a listed purpose (VTI-ACL-109). A registered name is never an IRI, because it contains no `:`.
Purpose.title: Purpose

RecordPurpose.description: The one purpose for which a caller will use room content a request discloses (VTI-ACL-103): a name registered in the VTI specification's purpose registry (`personalisation`, `taskExecution`, `analytics`, `modelTraining`) or an absolute IRI. Granted only as the caller's authority grants it — `any` grants every purpose but `modelTraining` — refused otherwise (`purposeNotGranted`), and recorded with the read. Distinct from `PermittedUse`, which is what a record's author permits and is a statement, not a grant.
RecordPurpose.title: RecordPurpose

schema.description: An agent asks the party holding its principal's room keys to open one sealed record. The key never crosses to the agent: this is a decryption oracle, not a key-release call.

key.description: The record's key within the room.

purpose.description: OPTIONAL. The one purpose the caller will use the content this request discloses for (VTI-ACL-103), as `RecordPurpose` defines it. A purpose not granted is refused with `purposeNotGranted`. May be omitted where exactly one purpose is granted, or `any`.

roomId.description: The room the record belongs to. Part of the record's associated data, so a caller naming the wrong room gets an authentication failure rather than someone else's plaintext.

sealed.description: The sealed record exactly as the host returned it.

epoch.description: The epoch it was sealed under. The oracle refuses an epoch it holds no key for rather than guessing.

version.description: The record's version. Bound into the associated data, so a record served at a different version does not open.
